title.narrative: Meeting the Immediate lifesaving Needs to foster the resilience of vulnerable population affected by Ein El Helwi conflict

description.narrative: ltpgtMeeting the emergency basic food needs and building resilience of 1,175 displaced individuals and families in conflict areas—comprising of 937 PRL, 183 Lebanese, 24 PRS, 19 SRS, and 12 migrants—ensures access to basic necessities, including food, hygiene, and protection cash. This initiative will help alleviate their increased vulnerability and severe food insecurity caused by protracted displacement. The eight-month project is designed in an integrated manner to meet the objectives of the Ein El Hilwe emergency plan and to complement services provided by other partners and agencies, thereby avoiding duplication of assistance.ltbrgtThe project has two main components: food security and protection, addressing the most pressing needs of Ein El Hilwe. For example, security concerns in southern Lebanon, along with their psychological and economic impacts, have exacerbated and complicated the crisis for all residents.ltbrgtThe direct 1,175 beneficiary households will be identified from a pool of 2,950 through a vulnerability assessment, with priority given to displaced families meeting 6 out of the following 8 criteria:ltbrgt- Displaced family either hosted or renting a house inside or outside the camp.ltbrgt- Not included within the MPCA.ltbrgt- Large households with 5 or more members.ltbrgt- Households headed by women with four or more children, including a person with special needs (PWSN).ltbrgt- The breadwinner is jobless or unable to work due to age, illness, disability, or has lost their job due to economic deterioration or security reasons.ltbrgt- Households with pregnant or lactating women.ltbrgt- Households with high medical costs.ltbrgtThrough this project, 305 female headed HHs will be included in three PSS sessions. From these 305 HHs, 60 will be selected to receive cash for protection, with an average of two payments. ltbrgtThe project builds on the work of the emergency response coordination group established during the conflict in Ein el Hilwe, managed by UNRWA. Nabaa has provided vital information to international organizations and UNRWA on the most vulnerable individuals affected by the war, refining action plans for displaced families still living in conflict zones within the Ein el Hilwe camp.ltbrgtThe project's progress continues the trajectory set in early August, with two phases of armed conflict resulting in internal displacement, and the establishment of four UNRWA emergency accommodation centers. The Emergency Coordination Group was formed in response to urgent humanitarian needs. Nabaa played a pivotal role by managing two displacement centers and conducting two pieces of research: one on the extent of damage caused by the civil war in Ein El Hilwe, and the second focusing on families displaced and hosted both outside and inside the camp.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
